summary: Radar for 2026-11-22, GLP-1 focus. The biggest early chance is the two oral GLP-1 pills now reaching pharmacy shelves in Australia, and the confusion over which one to choose. Foundayo was registered by the TGA on 16 Nov, has no rules about food timing, and supplies are expected "within days". The Wegovy pill is already in pharmacies and must be taken on an empty stomach with a wait before eating. The Australian, SMH and the Herald Sun are all asking whether the pills work as well as injections. Our Foundayo Short got 826 views on day 1. We should ship the held Foundayo what-to-expect video now and follow it with a label-only "Foundayo vs Wegovy pill vs tirzepatide" head-to-head. The second chance is the broad question "why tirzepatide works differently for different people". ScienceDaily and SciTechDaily picked it up on 19–21 Nov, but the source is a Conversation explainer about a study that hasn't run yet, so trial averages in the full population have to carry the content. Third: muscle loss. SMH's "lost 10kg of muscle" story (22 Nov) plus MarketWatch and ThinkPol on the T-REx strength-training trial give a fresh hook to retitle Bones as "Muscle Loss: How Much in the Trials?". Thanksgiving is at its peak, four days out; keep the 20:00 holiday Shorts linked to the Thanksgiving video. PBS and US News both ran feast guides. The NAION label change has peaked in news, but the evergreen "Serious Risks: How Rare?" long video gets a fresh boost from AU searches for "glp-1 chronic weight management risks". The required search-demand formats are all included: pen how-to and injection sites, months 2–6, label changes, head-to-heads against tirzepatide, and felt symptoms (hair loss, nausea, still full the morning after, heartburn). Retatrutide's knee-pain results (TRIUMPH-4, NEJM 8 Nov) are a real randomized result for a drug people search, but it isn't approved, so it's marked caution with a trial-result angle only. Rejected: prices of compounded tirzepatide (FlatRx), peptide and black-market stories, employer coverage and access, the Lilly and Novo stock stories, the "GLP-1 vacation" story, child and teen trials as lead topics, and observational cancer and pancreatitis-severity claims as standalone topics.

candidates.topic: Foundayo (orforglipron) pill: what to expect, from the label, as it reaches Australian pharmacies after TGA registration on 16 Nov
candidates.angle: Ship the held 11-22 long video once its known faults are fixed (the silent closing scene and the 0.02 masking limit). Close with the line to talk to your prescriber about whether it's right for you.

candidates.topic: Foundayo vs the Wegovy pill vs tirzepatide injections: what's different (label head-to-head)
candidates.angle: Lead with the felt difference. The Wegovy pill needs an empty stomach and a wait before you eat or drink. Foundayo has no food-timing rule. Then give each drug's label weight-loss figure from its own trial population. Say clearly that no randomized head-to-head between them exists yet, and give tirzepatide's SURMOUNT-1 figure as the reference point. No prices and no advice on which to choose.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) weight loss: why doesn't it work the same for everyone?
candidates.angle: A broad, searched question. Give the SURMOUNT-1 averages by arm in the full trial population, then show the spread: some people lost much more and some much less. Then the factors the trials link to response, with type 2 diabetes being the clearest one (SURMOUNT-2 losses were smaller). Name metabolic adaptation as an open research question; the Alberta study hasn't run yet. No dose advice, and an encouraging framing: a smaller loss can still be meaningful for health.
